claim: The hexosamine biosynthetic pathway (HBP) consumes about 2%–3% of cellular glucose.
source: The hexosamine biosynthetic pathway (HBP) is an anabolic branch of glycolysis consuming about 2%–3% of cellular glucose (Marshall et al., 1991; Ghosh et al., 1960).
evidence: Supported by citations to Marshall et al., 1991 and Ghosh et al., 1960

claim: The HBP has been strongly associated with stress resistance and longevity.
source: It provides substrates for various posttranslational modification (PTM) reactions and has been strongly associated with stress resistance and longevity as well as cell growth and transformation (Denzel et al., 2014; Wellen et al., 2010; Yamashita et al., 1985).
evidence: Supported by citations to Denzel et al., 2014; Wellen et al., 2010; Yamashita et al., 1985

claim: The HBP has been strongly associated with cell growth and transformation.
source: It provides substrates for various posttranslational modification (PTM) reactions and has been strongly associated with stress resistance and longevity as well as cell growth and transformation (Denzel et al., 2014; Wellen et al., 2010; Yamashita et al., 1985).
evidence: Supported by citations to Denzel et al., 2014; Wellen et al., 2010; Yamashita et al., 1985

claim: GFPT converts fructose-6-phosphate (Frc6P) and L-glutamine (L-Gln) to D-glucosamine-6-phosphate (GlcN6P) in the first and rate limiting step of the HBP.
source: In the first and rate limiting step of the HBP, glutamine fructose-6-phosphate amidotransferase (GFPT) converts fructose-6-phosphate (Frc6P) and L-glutamine (L-Gln) to D-glucosamine-6-phosphate (GlcN6P) (Ghosh et al., 1960).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ghosh et al., 1960

claim: The two mammalian GFPT paralogs GFPT1 and GFPT2 show 75%–80% amino acid sequence identity.
source: The two mammalian GFPT paralogs GFPT1 and GFPT2 show 75%–80% amino acid sequence identity (Oki et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citation to Oki et al., 1999

claim: GFPT1 is ubiquitously expressed.
source: While GFPT1 is ubiquitously expressed, GFPT2 is reported to be predominantly expressed in the nervous system.
evidence: Statement made in the manuscript text

claim: GFPT2 is predominantly expressed in the nervous system.
source: While GFPT1 is ubiquitously expressed, GFPT2 is reported to be predominantly expressed in the nervous system.
evidence: Statement made in the manuscript text

claim: GlcN6P can be converted to Frc6P by glucosamine-6-phosphate deaminase 1 and 2 (GNPDA1/2).
source: Notably, GlcN6P can be converted to Frc6P by glucosamine-6-phosphate deaminase 1 and 2 (GNPDA1/2), shunting metabolites back into glycolysis (Arreola et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Arreola et al., 2003

claim: Glucosamine-phosphate N-acetyltransferase (GNA1) acetylates GlcN6P to N-acetylglucosamine-6-phosphate (GlcNAc-6P) using acetyl-CoA as the acetyl donor.
source: In the second step of the HBP, glucosamine-phosphate N-acetyltransferase (GNA1) acetylates GlcN6P to N-acetylglucosamine-6-phosphate (GlcNAc-6P) using acetyl-CoA as the acetyl donor (Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2008

claim: The acetylation reaction by GNA1 is presumed to be reversible through deacetylation of GlcNAc6P.
source: This reaction is also presumed to be reversible through deacetylation of GlcNAc6P (Weidanz et al., 1996; Bergfeld et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Weidanz et al., 1996; Bergfeld et al., 2012

claim: GlcNAc-6P is isomerized into GlcNAc-1-phosphate (GlcNAc-1P) by GlcNAc phosphomutase (PGM3).
source: After isomerization into GlcNAc-1-phosphate (GlcNAc-1P) mediated by GlcNAc phosphomutase (PGM3), UTP is used in a final step by UDP-N-acetylglucosamine pyrophosphorylase (UAP1) to synthesize the final product uridine 5′-diphosphate-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (UDP-GlcNAc) (Ricciardiello et al., 2018; Mio et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ricciardiello et al., 2018; Mio et al., 1998

claim: UDP-N-acetylglucosamine pyrophosphorylase (UAP1) uses UTP to synthesize UDP-GlcNAc from GlcNAc-1P.
source: After isomerization into GlcNAc-1-phosphate (GlcNAc-1P) mediated by GlcNAc phosphomutase (PGM3), UTP is used in a final step by UDP-N-acetylglucosamine pyrophosphorylase (UAP1) to synthesize the final product uridine 5′-diphosphate-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (UDP-GlcNAc) (Ricciardiello et al., 2018; Mio et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ricciardiello et al., 2018; Mio et al., 1998

claim: UDP-GlcNAc can be reversibly interconverted to UDP-GalNAc by the enzyme UDP-galactose-4′-epimerase (GALE).
source: UDP-GlcNAc can be reversibly interconverted to its epimer uridine 5′-diphosphate-N-acetyl-D-galactosamine (UDP-GalNAc) by the enzyme UDP-galactose-4′-epimerase (GALE) and the pool of both metabolites is termed UDP-HexNAc (Thoden et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to Thoden et al., 2001

claim: The HBP is the only source for UDP-GlcNAc.
source: The HBP is the only source for UDP-GlcNAc and relies on substrates from carbon, nitrogen, fatty-acid, and energy metabolism.
evidence: Statement made in the manuscript text

claim: The HBP relies on substrates from carbon, nitrogen, fatty-acid, and energy metabolism.
source: The HBP is the only source for UDP-GlcNAc and relies on substrates from carbon, nitrogen, fatty-acid, and energy metabolism.
evidence: Statement made in the manuscript text

claim: The HBP is optimally positioned as a metabolic sensor that can modulate downstream cellular signaling through UDP-GlcNAc dependent PTMs.
source: It is therefore optimally positioned as a metabolic sensor that can modulate downstream cellular signaling through UDP-GlcNAc dependent PTMs (Marshall et al., 1991).
evidence: Supported by citation to Marshall et al., 1991

claim: UDP-GlcNAc is a precursor of chitin, peptidoglycans, and glycosaminoglycans.
source: UDP-GlcNAc is a precursor of several important biomolecules, such as chitin, peptidoglycans, and glycosaminoglycans, and for a number of dynamic glycosylation events.
evidence: Statement made in the manuscript text

claim: Mucin-type O-glycosylation plays an important role in the extracellular matrix.
source: Mucin-type O-glycosylation plays an important role in the extracellular matrix (Hanisch, 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hanisch, 2001

claim: N-linked-glycosylation orchestrates protein folding in the endoplasmic reticulum.
source: N-linked-glycosylation orchestrates protein folding in the endoplasmic reticulum and is therefore crucial in protein homeostasis (Parodi, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Parodi, 2000

claim: N-linked-glycosylation is crucial in protein homeostasis.
source: N-linked-glycosylation orchestrates protein folding in the endoplasmic reticulum and is therefore crucial in protein homeostasis (Parodi, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Parodi, 2000

claim: N-glycans contribute to the cell surface glycocalyx as structural components of proteins.
source: N-glycans further contribute to the cell surface glycocalyx as structural components of proteins (Martinez-Seara Monne et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Martinez-Seara Monne et al., 2013

claim: O-GlcNAcylation is the addition of single GlcNAc moieties to Thr/Ser residues.
source: Finally, the addition of single GlcNAc moieties to Thr/Ser residues, termed O-GlcNAcylation, occurs dynamically on hundreds of proteins, thus modulating a variety of downstream pathways (Hart, 1997).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hart, 1997

claim: O-GlcNAcylation occurs dynamically on hundreds of proteins.
source: Finally, the addition of single GlcNAc moieties to Thr/Ser residues, termed O-GlcNAcylation, occurs dynamically on hundreds of proteins, thus modulating a variety of downstream pathways (Hart, 1997).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hart, 1997

claim: O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) is the single protein that accomplishes O-GlcNAcylation.
source: Surprisingly, this dynamic PTM is accomplished by a single protein, O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) is the only known enzyme to remove O-GlcNAc modifications (Haltiwanger et al., 1992; Dong and Hart, 1994).
evidence: Supported by citations to Haltiwanger et al., 1992; Dong and Hart, 1994

claim: O-GlcNAcase (OGA) is the only known enzyme to remove O-GlcNAc modifications.
source: Surprisingly, this dynamic PTM is accomplished by a single protein, O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT), and O-GlcNAcase (OGA) is the only known enzyme to remove O-GlcNAc modifications (Haltiwanger et al., 1992; Dong and Hart, 1994).
evidence: Supported by citations to Haltiwanger et al., 1992; Dong and Hart, 1994

claim: Glycosylation reactions are limited by intracellular UDP-GlcNAc.
source: While it is known that these glycosylation reactions are limited by intracellular UDP-GlcNAc, how the HBP is regulated to adapt UDP-GlcNAc levels according to nutrient availability is poorly understood.
evidence: Statement made in the manuscript text

claim: Alterations in UDP-GlcNAc abundance can have detrimental effects resulting in pathological conditions like diabetes, cancer, cardiovascular diseases, and neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Due to the diverse function of UDP-GlcNAc, alterations in its abundance can have detrimental effects resulting in pathological conditions like diabetes, cancer, cardiovascular diseases, and neurodegenerative diseases (Marshall et al., 1991; Oikari et al., 2018; Arnold et al., 1996; Champattanachai et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Marshall et al., 1991; Oikari et al., 2018; Arnold et al., 1996; Champattanachai et al., 2007

claim: TM resistant mutants in C. elegans were enriched for longevity.
source: In a previous chemical mutagenesis screen in Caenorhabditis elegans, we isolated mutants resistant to the toxin tunicamycin (TM) as a proxy for enhanced protein quality control and found that TM resistant mutants were enriched for longevity (Denzel et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Denzel et al., 2014

claim: TM is a competitive inhibitor of UDPGlcNAc:dolichylphosphate GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase (GPT).
source: TM is a competitive inhibitor of UDPGlcNAc:dolichylphosphate GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase (GPT), which catalyzes the first step of Nglycan synthesis utilizing UDP-GlcNAc (Heifetz et al., 1979).
evidence: Supported by citation to Heifetz et al., 1979

claim: TM disrupts N-glycosylation and leads to proteins misfolding and proteotoxic stress.
source: TM thus disrupts N-glycosylation and leads to proteins misfolding and proteotoxic stress (Parodi, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Parodi, 2000

claim: Single amino acid substitutions in GFPT1 result in gain-of-function due to loss of UDP-GlcNAc feedback inhibition.
source: We found that single amino acid substitutions in GFPT1 result in gain-of-function (GOF) due to loss of UDP-GlcNAc feedback inhibition, elevating cellular UDP-GlcNAc levels and thereby counteracting TM toxicity (Ruegenberg et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ruegenberg et al., 2020

claim: GFPT1 GOF mutations elevate cellular UDP-GlcNAc levels and counteract TM toxicity.
source: We found that single amino acid substitutions in GFPT1 result in gain-of-function (GOF) due to loss of UDP-GlcNAc feedback inhibition, elevating cellular UDP-GlcNAc levels and thereby counteracting TM toxicity (Ruegenberg et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ruegenberg et al., 2020

claim: Introducing the GFPT1 GOF mutation in N2a cells confirmed a conserved mechanism.
source: By introducing the same GOF mutation in GFPT1 of mouse neuroblastoma Neuro2a (N2a) cells, we confirmed a conserved mechanism (Horn et al., 2020), suggesting that screening for TM resistance might be a suitable unbiased means to analyze the HBP through genetic approaches in mammalian cells.
evidence: Supported by citation to Horn et al., 2020

claim: 27 million AN3-12 mouse embryonic stem cells were used for mutagenesis in the TM resistance screen.
source: In order to reach a high degree of saturation, 27 million AN3-12 mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) were used for mutagenesis.
evidence: Statement made in the manuscript text describing the experimental procedure

claim: CRISPR/Cas9-generated AMDHD2 KO mutants showed a significant increase in UDP-GlcNAc concentrations.
